activities.anchor: collapses on its own edge cases
activities.caption: pair each school with its test of validity
activities.name: jurSchoolsMatch

config.prompt: What makes a rule law? Pair each school with its answer:

pairs.right: the rule of recognition — an accepted social practice among officials
an internal morality of form: publicity, prospectivity, clarity
principles, not just rules — judges construct a coherent moral story
an unjust rule is not law (lex iniusta non est lex)

config.why: The separation thesis: a rule's legal validity and its moral merit are separate questions — "bad law is still law", and must be obeyed or repealed lawfully.

activities.caption: drag the divider — mirror, then lag
activities.name: jurMirrorCompare

config.prompt: Law tracks society in two directions — drag the divider:

before.label: The mirror: law codifying moved consensus
before.text: The Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013 and the indoor smoking ban (Health Act 2006, in force 2007) codified shifts that surveys and public-health data had already made.

after.label: The lag: consensus waiting on law
after.text: Homosexuality was partially decriminalised only in 1967 (Sexual Offences Act) — a decade after the Wolfenden Report recommended it.

config.why: The discipline implied: statutes as social engineering — instruments with measurable social effects, and the effects feed back into reform. If validity is a social practice (Hart), content cannot be studied apart from the society sustaining it.

activities.anchor: won most of the scholarly field
activities.caption: run the Hart–Devlin structure on a live controversy
activities.name: jurDevlinBranch

config.root: A minister proposes criminalising a practice a majority finds distasteful but that harms no one else. You have the template.

choices.label: Whose harm is claimed?
choices.feedback: Hart's move: deploy Mill's harm principle — disgust is not damage.

choices.label: Whose morality is being enforced?
choices.feedback: Devlin's premise: a shared morality holds society together — but see the next probe.

choices.label: What evidence exists that the fabric actually tears?
choices.feedback: The empirical demand that unsettled Devlin's position.

harm.text: No identifiable victim. The enforcement case must rest on morality alone — probe it.

choices.label: Is the shared morality concept precise enough to legislate on?
choices.feedback: Hart's second point: its imprecision makes it a shaky trigger.

morality.text: A majority's moral feeling. Devlin says attacks on it threaten the social fabric itself.

choices.label: Demand the evidence of tearing
choices.feedback: The structure always ends here: identify the harm, name the morality, test the fabric.

fabric.text: Hart's 1963 reply — harm principle plus the imprecision of "shared morality" — won the scholarly field and, eventually, the legislative one. The same three probes now run on abortion, assisted dying and drugs.

config.why: The transferable skill is the structure, not the verdict: whose harm, whose morality, does the fabric tear.

activities.anchor: and some of it knowingly licenses immorality
activities.caption: file each item in the law–morality overlap map
activities.name: jurMoralBuckets

config.prompt: Law and morality intersect but do not coincide — file each item:

items.label: limitation periods that bar meritorious claims
limitation periods and service rules as such

config.why: Most of law is morally indifferent, a sliver knowingly licenses immorality — and the Hart–Devlin argument is about exactly where the enforced subset ends.

config.prompt: How many statutory instruments does Westminster churn out per year (roughly)?
config.why: About three thousand — most of the law citizens actually live under (fees, benefit rates, speed limits) is delegated, made by ministers, not the sovereign legislature. The enabling-act problem — sharpened by Germany's Enabling Act of 1933 — is why scrutiny safeguards and ultra vires review are structural necessities.
config.context: Accountability is procedural: the Joint Committee on Statutory Instruments, negative or affirmative resolutions.

activities.anchor: Words fail; interpretation is where jurisprudence meets daily practice
activities.caption: find the mislabelled rung on the ladder
activities.name: jurInterpSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary mislabels the ladder — click it:
lines: The literal rule reads plain meaning — Whitely v Chappell: impersonating a dead voter is no offence.
The golden rule modifies absurdity — Re Sigsworth 1935: the murderer son forfeited the inheritance.
The mischief rule fixes the gap the Act targeted — Smith v Hughes 1960: balcony solicitation fell within the Act's mischief.
Pepper v Hart 1993 admitted parliamentary materials in narrow cases — under the literal rule.
Every approach embeds a theory: interpretation is legislation's continuation by other means.
config.correction: Pepper v Hart reinforced the purposive approach — the modern rung, not the literal one.
config.why: Presumptions (against retrospectivity, against penalising without fault) and the rules of language ride alongside all four rungs.

activities.caption: pair each term of precedent's grammar with its force
activities.name: jurPrecedentMatch

config.prompt: Precedent's grammar — pair each term with its force:

pairs.right: the reason for the decision — it binds
said by the way — it persuades but does not bind
the facts genuinely differ, so the rule does not reach this case
reserved to higher courts, or the same court per the Practice Statement 1966
the marital rape exemption abolished by reinterpretation — a century of law changed in a judgment

config.why: The hierarchy is mechanical — the Supreme Court binds all below (but not itself since 1966); the Court of Appeal binds below it save the Young v Bristol Aeroplane 1944 exceptions.

activities.anchor: a remarkable hit rate for unelected drafting
activities.caption: place the Law Commission's uptake share
activities.name: jurReformPlace

config.prompt: The Law Commission (established 1965): what share of its recommendations have historically been implemented?
config.why: Around two-thirds — consultation papers, reports with draft Bills; parliamentary time is the bottleneck, which is why the Commission's independence and government uptake are themselves rule-of-law indicators.
